title: Cucumber and BDD
subtitle: Nine cards on specs everyone can read, before the full lesson.

cards.headline: The test is the conversation, written down.
cards.body: BDD is not a testing tool. It is a way of agreeing what software should do, in examples, before anyone writes code. Cucumber just keeps those examples honest.

cards.headline: Three activities, in order
points: Discovery: the three amigos map examples
Automation: step definitions make them run

cards.headline: Given, When, Then is a grammar for behaviour
cards.body: Feature files, Backgrounds, Outlines, Rules and tags, and how JUnit runs them and reports back. One map you rebuild from memory.

cards.headline: A good scenario says what, never how
cards.body: Declarative steps, one behaviour per scenario, no clicking through screens. Ten review decisions on real-looking scenarios.

cards.headline: Most BDD failures are not technical
cards.body: A team adopted Cucumber and got slow, brittle tests nobody reads. Investigate what really went wrong, and what the tool was blamed for.

cards.headline: Suite maths

number.label: flakiness per step is enough to make a 20-step scenario fail most of the time

cards.body: Play with retries, UI versus API steps, parallel runs and exploding Outlines.

quote.text: If the feature file lies, the suite fails. That is the whole trick.

cards.headline: What this lesson covers
cards.body: Tap any line to jump back to its card.

cards.headline: Start with the map
cards.body: Chapter 1 lays the whole system out on one map you will rebuild from memory.
